controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so that solve(data) implements the user contract exactly. The current file does a shallow merge and fails the nested-object case (base {a:{x:1}}, patch {a:{y:2}} must give {a:{x:1,y:2}}). Requirements: validate that data is a dict with JSON-object 'base' and 'patch', else raise ValueError. Deep-merge patch into base: for each patch key, if value is null remove the key (no-op if absent); if both base and patch values are objects, merge recursively; if both are lists, the patch list replaces the base list; if base key is absent, insert the patch value as is; otherwise if the JSON types differ (booleans and numbers are distinct types; objects, lists, strings, booleans, numbers are each their own type) raise ValueError. Otherwise (same type, scalar) the patch value replaces the base value. Result key order: base keys in original order, then patch-only keys in patch order. Never mutate inputs (use copies). Python standard library only; no I/O, no dynamic code execution, and only the allowed imports. Write only module.py.

Write test_cases.json only. It must be a JSON list of at least four distinct cases for solve(data) implementing the deep-merge contract. Each case has an input object with keys base and patch, plus exactly one of output (expected JSON result) or error (exception class name, e.g. ValueError). Optional name/notes fields are allowed. Cover: nested object merge (base {a:{x:1}}, patch {a:{y:2}} gives {a:{x:1,y:2}}); null removes a key and removing an absent key is a no-op; list replacement with no concatenation; boolean vs number type mismatch raises ValueError; non-object base or patch raises ValueError; key order (base order first, then patch-only keys in patch order). Expected values must follow the user contract exactly, not the current module.py behavior. Do not write module.py.
